ai.description: *Calodactylodes aureus* reaches 10–12 cm. It is golden-yellow with dark brown dorsal spots and a pale underside. Key features include large, circular eyes and specialized, expanded toe pads.
ai.identificationRemarks: The Indian Golden Gecko is best distinguished by the prominent, golden-yellow spots or patches along its back, which contrast sharply against a darker, brownish body.
ai.habitat: The Indian Golden Gecko inhabits rocky outcrops and boulder-strewn terrain within dry deciduous forests, typically at elevations ranging from 200 to 1,000 meters.
ai.behavior: The Indian Golden Gecko is strictly nocturnal, spending its nights foraging for insects on vertical rock faces and tree trunks within its specialized forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Calodactylodes aureus* is oviparous, laying a clutch of two hard-shelled eggs in rock crevices. Breeding typically occurs between March and August.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Indian Golden Gecko is endemic to the rocky hill forests of the Eastern Ghats in Andhra Pradesh and Odisha, typically occurring at elevations up to 1,000 meters.
